proposals.before: Shizhi served Emperor Jing for over a year as chancellor of Huainan, still on account of the earlier offense.
proposals.after: Shizhi served Emperor Jing for over a year; he was made chancellor of Huainan, still on account of the earlier offense.
proposals.reason: Chinese 事景帝歲餘，為淮南相 means he served Jing for over a year and then was made Huainan chancellor; the literal fuses the tenure into the Huainan post.

proposals.before: Just then the Xiongnu had struck deep into Chaona and slain Sun Ang, the commandant of Beidi.
proposals.after: Just then the Xiongnu had struck deep into Chaona and slain Ang, the commandant of Beidi.
proposals.reason: Chinese names only 卬 (Ang); the idiomatic invents the surname Sun not present in the source.

proposals.before: In his bearing he resembled the old lords of Wei who won the people's love.
proposals.after: His forebears had enjoyed favor with the ancient lord of Wei.
proposals.reason: Chinese 其行有寵於古之衛君也 (cf. usual 其先) is about ancestral favor with the Wei lord, not that Ji An's bearing resembled Wei lords.

proposals.before: As grand minister of finance he let contractors use his clients as labor; the accounts fell deep into arrears.
proposals.after: As grand minister of agriculture he let contractors use his clients as labor; the accounts fell deep into arrears.
proposals.reason: Chinese 大司農 is the grand minister of agriculture, matching the literal and s0287; 'finance' mislabels the office.

proposals.before: His conduct had favor with the ancient lord of Wei.
proposals.after: His forebears had enjoyed favor with the ancient lord of Wei.
proposals.reason: The corrected source reads 其先, 'his forebears,' not 其行, 'his conduct'; the literal field must follow the attested text.

decisions.reason: 事景帝歲餘 and 為淮南相 are sequential clauses: Shizhi served Jing over a year, then was made Huainan chancellor; the original wrongly fuses the Jing tenure into the Huainan office.
This unit writes only 卬, but the Beidi commandant is 孫卬: Shiji 惠景間侯者年表 names 北地都尉孫卬, and Xu Guang on the Xiongnu biography notes 姓孫. The idiomatic surname is historically accurate, not an invention.

The dossier reading 其行 is corrupt; standard Hanshu (and Shiji) has 其先有寵於古之衛君也—ancestral favor with the ancient Wei lord. The original invents resemblance and popular love; the repair restores the sense, and the next unit on ten generations of office supports the ancestral reading.
